learning_outcomes.text: Explain fundamental concepts of reliability, safety, availability, and maintainability.
Describe mechanical failure processes and associated statistical models.
Characterize reliability functions, failure rates, and probabilistic models (Weibull, log-normal, exponential).
Explain methods for estimating lifespan and engineering criteria for durable design.
Identify testing and monitoring procedures for the reliability of mechanical systems.
Utilize statistical methods for reliability data analysis.
Apply prediction models to determine lifespan and failure risks.
Develop block diagrams, reliability models, and FMEA/FMECA analyses.
Use specialized software for reliability calculation and failure simulation.
Propose technical solutions to increase durability and reduce maintenance interventions.
Work responsibly in data analysis, respecting ethical and professional principles.
Demonstrate autonomy in technical documentation and in the use of analytical tools.
Integrate safety and reliability criteria into engineering decisions.
Actively contribute to multidisciplinary teams, providing solid interpretations of risks and performance.
Develop professional competences for continuous improvement of design and operation processes.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the reliability of mechanical systems
Engineering analysis methods: FMEA, FMECA, Fault Tree
Determination of lifespan and failure risk
Analysis and modeling of the reliability of a complex system
teaching_methods: Visual presentations, graphs, mathematical schemes and industry examples
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Grades will be awarded as integers from 1 to 10. A grade of 5 certifies the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits.
